verdict: AVGO Q3 AI guide miss triggers sector wipeout (-10% PHLX Jun 5); recovery underway but HBM YoY price decline and whisper-miss pattern signal the easy multiple-expansion phase for AI semis may be ending — demand intact, margin compression ahead.
body_md:
## Fresh developments (last 24-72h)

**Sector sell-off + partial recovery (Jun 3-13):** AVGO's Jun 3 Q2 earnings beat revenue (2.2B, +48% YoY, AI semi +143%) but Q3 AI semiconductor guide of **6B undershot the ~7.2B whisper** by ~7%. This triggered a Jun 5-6 sector rout: PHLX -10%, AVGO -12.6%, MRVL -17%, AMD -10.9%, INTC -11.3% — erasing ~.4T in market cap, worst single-day chip loss since March 2020. Recovery began Jun 8-10 (MU +9.9%, NVDA +1.7%). As of Jun 13-14, sector is in post-shock stabilization.

**MRVL Computex surge (Jun 2):** Jensen Huang called Marvell "the next trillion-dollar company" on stage at Computex, sending MRVL +32.5% — its biggest one-day gain ever. The subsequent sector crash (-17% Jun 5) offset most of the gain. MRVL also added to S&P 500 effective Jun 22.

**DRAM Q1 confirmed; HBM YoY decline emerging:** TrendForce confirmed DRAM industry revenue +81% QoQ in Q1-2026. Q2 conventional DRAM guide still +58-63% QoQ. However, **HBM contract prices are now in YoY decline** due to competition across all three suppliers — the baseline correction signal is arriving early, while physical 2026 supply remains sold out.

**Solar pullback (Jun 5-9):** FSLR -8%, ARRY -6.1%, NXT -5.5% on policy/tariff uncertainty. Section 232 polysilicon tariff clarity expected by end of June. FSLR CdTe structure provides partial insulation; South Carolina fab opening H2-2026 keeps long thesis intact.

**HIVE (Jun 11):** Bullish analyst targets reiterated; HPC ARR now 5M anchored by 0M 2-yr GPU cloud contract (Feb 2026) deploying 504 Nvidia B200s. Pathway to 60M ARR by 2028 via planned 100K-GPU GTA facility.

**No fresh developments (last 48h):** MU — next catalyst is Jun 24 earnings (options pricing ~20% move, consensus EPS +932% YoY). LITE, CIEN, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU — no stock-moving news detected.

---

---

## Context vs baseline

- **AVGO guide miss is the key new data point**: Only ~7% below the whisper but enough to wipe 10% off the index — confirms AI semi valuations were pricing perfection. Demand cycle is intact; pace of upside revision is decelerating.
- **HBM correction signal activating early**: HBM prices in YoY decline while 2026 physically sold out. Three-way HBM4 race (SKH ~60-70% of Vera Rubin allocation, Micron 10-15%) is compressing unit economics even as volumes grow. Baseline thesis on post-2026 correction is playing out on schedule.
- **Capex ceiling still rising**: Aggregate hyperscaler capex raised again to ~25-750B (Meta raised to 25-145B). No guide-down from any hyperscaler.
- **MRVL/AVGO custom ASIC duopoly**: Together control ~95% of custom AI ASIC co-design. MRVL projects 1B AI ASIC revenue FY2026. Jensen endorsement + S&P 500 add are structural, not just sentiment.
- **Optical intact**: COHR Q3 FY26 beat (.81B, +21% YoY); InP 70% supply gap persists; ALAB +93% YoY, CRDO +272% YoY.

---

## Signals flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Conventional DRAM pricing Q2 | +58-63% QoQ | Bull |
| HBM unit pricing (YoY trend) | YoY decline beginning | Bear (vs baseline) |
| Hyperscaler AI capex | Raised to ~25-750B | Bull |
| AVGO Q3 AI guide vs whisper | Miss (6B vs 7.2B) | Bear near-term |
| MRVL custom ASIC position | Jensen endorsement + S&P add | Bull |
| Optical supply/InP tightness | Structural shortage persists | Bull COHR/ALAB/CRDO |
| Solar/US policy | Section 232 tariff clarity pending | Bear near-term, watch end-June |

---

## Most important development

**AVGO's Q3 AI guide miss vs the whisper number** is the dominant event of the week. It is not a demand-collapse signal — hyperscaler capex keeps rising — but it exposed how much perfection was priced into AI semis. Simultaneously, **HBM prices entering YoY decline while physically sold out** is the first hard data point validating the baseline correction-risk thesis. The market is beginning to price the transition from price-driven memory supercycle gains to volume-only growth: unit economics compress even as the physical ramp continues.

Not investment advice. Forward figures are forecasts.
